Write a table of models into a folder to fit on a cluster

Source: R/hpc.R
write_hpc_bundle.Rd

Writes what is needed to fit the models of a table built with build_hazard_models() on a cluster that schedules its jobs with Slurm, such as those of the Digital Research Alliance of Canada, into one folder, the bundle. The bundle is then copied to the cluster, where the scripts it contains install what it needs (install.sh) and check it (check.sh, which calls check_hpc_bundle()).

Usage

write_hpc_bundle(
  models,
  long,
  dir,
  account,
  observation = c("interval", "continuous", "mixed"),
  unit = NULL,
  kfold = FALSE,
  K = NULL,
  rhat = 1.01,
  ess = 400,
  divergent = 0.001,
  time = "12:00:00",
  mem_per_cpu = "4000M",
  email = NULL,
  modules = c("StdEnv/2023", "r/4.5.0"),
  r_library = NULL,
  remote = NULL,
  rtft_source = NULL,
  template = "alliance",
  ...
)

Arguments

models

A data frame, the table of models from build_hazard_models().

long

A data frame, the table of intervals at risk from build_hazard_data(), to which every model is fitted.

dir

A character string, the folder to write the bundle into. It is created if it does not exist, and must be empty if it does.

account

A character string, the allocation the jobs are charged to, as Slurm's --account takes it (for example "def-someone").

observation

A character string, how the failure times were observed, as in fit_hazard().

unit

An optional character string, the unit to leave out in cross-validation, as in loo_hazard(). NULL (the default) chooses it as loo_hazard() does.

kfold

A single logical value. TRUE also cross-validates each model by refitting, one task per model and fold. Defaults to FALSE.

K

An optional single whole number, the number of folds when kfold is TRUE, as in kfold_hazard(). NULL (the default) gives one fold per unit. With fewer folds than units the units are assigned to folds at random, once; call set.seed() first to get the same folds again.

rhat, ess, divergent

The limits of the sampling rule, as in fit_hazard_models().

time

A character string, the time each task may run, as Slurm's --time takes it: hours, minutes and seconds ("12:00:00", the default), or days first ("1-12:00:00"). A task that runs past it is stopped and its work is lost. The allocation is charged for the time a task ran, times its cores, and not for the time asked; a longer time can mean a longer wait in the queue.

mem_per_cpu

A character string, the memory for each core, with its unit, as Slurm's --mem-per-cpu takes it. Defaults to "4000M", about the memory per core of the Alliance's standard nodes, so asking it costs no more than the cores do; asking more is charged as more cores. Slurm reads "4G" as 4096 M, which the clusters of the Alliance point out at each submission.

email

An optional character string, the address Slurm writes to when a task fails. NULL (the default) sends no mail.

modules

A character vector, the modules that give R on the cluster. The default, c("StdEnv/2023", "r/4.5.0"), is for the clusters of the Alliance; module avail r on the cluster lists the versions it offers.

r_library

An optional character string, the R library on the cluster that holds rTFT, brms and cmdstanr. NULL (the default) uses R's own personal library.

remote

An optional character string, where on the cluster to copy the bundle, as "user@host:folder" (for example "someone@nibi.alliancecan.ca:scratch/my-run"), without spaces. A folder written without a leading / is in your home folder on the cluster. It is used only to fill in the commands of README.txt and of the message, and nothing is sent to the cluster; NULL (the default) leaves placeholders there. The copy command creates the folder, with any folders above it that do not exist yet.

rtft_source

An optional character string, where the cluster installs rTFT from, as remotes::install_github() takes it. NULL (the default) uses the commit the installed rTFT came from, when it was installed from GitHub, or the tag of its release; a development version installed from a copy on your machine must be given, such as "eogmartins/rTFT@dev-0.2.0".

template

A character string, "alliance" (the default) for the scripts written for the clusters of the Alliance, or the path of a folder of your own holding settings.sh, install.sh, install.R, check.sh, submit.sh, task.sh, status.sh and README.txt, with the same placeholders. hpc_status() finds the log of a task as logs/<stage>-<array job>_<task>.out; a template that names its logs otherwise loses only the reason given for a task stopped by Slurm.

...

Further arguments for every fit, as in fit_hazard_models(), such as chains, iter, warmup, seed or control, or the priors that fit_hazard() takes.

Value

The path of the bundle, invisibly. A message says what was written and what to do next.

Details

Everything about the run is settled on the user's own machine, before anything is copied: the arguments are checked as fit_hazard_models() checks them, the unit left out in cross-validation is chosen and, with kfold = TRUE, the units are assigned to folds once for all the models. A mistake therefore is quickly found here and not on the cluster hours later.

The bundle holds:

  • settings.sh, the account, time, memory, cores and modules, written once and read by every script of the bundle. It is the one file to edit when a task needs more time or memory.

  • install.sh and install.R, which install what the bundle needs into the R of the cluster: rTFT at the version that wrote the bundle, from rtft_source, cmdstanr, and CmdStan. It is run once on each cluster, on the login node or, with bash install.sh --job, as a Slurm job.

  • check.sh, which checks the bundle and the R of the cluster on the login node.

  • submit.sh, which submits the tasks to Slurm as job arrays, one for the fits and one for the refits, queued to start when the fits have ended; task.sh, which Slurm runs for each task and which calls run_hpc_task(); and status.sh, which calls hpc_status() to say what each task has done.

  • README.txt, the steps to take, with the commands filled in.

  • inputs/, the data (data.rds), the models (models.rds), the settings of the run (settings.rds), the tasks as tables to read (tasks-fit.csv, and tasks-kfold.csv with kfold = TRUE), and checksums.txt, the checksum of each of these files, against which the cluster checks what it received.

  • stan/, results/ and logs/, empty, for the compiled models, the results and what each task prints.

The fits on the cluster use the cmdstanr backend, and each task runs its chains on as many cores as there are chains, so backend and cores cannot be given in ....

See also

check_hpc_bundle(), which checks the bundle on the cluster, hpc_status(), which says what its tasks have done, and collect_hpc(), which assembles their results.

Examples

# a small ramping assay in two trials (see fit_hazard())
path   <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = c(0, 60), temp = c(20, 35))
checks <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = seq(0, 60, by = 1))
ind    <- data.frame(id = 1:20, path_id = "A", event = 1,
                     trial = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
                     t_upper = sample(seq(10, 60, 10), 20, replace = TRUE))
long   <- build_hazard_data(ind, path, "interval", covariates = "trial",
                            checks = checks)
#> ℹ The intervals at risk were divided further, into 2570 rows from 870, so that
#>   temperature changes by at most 0.1 degrees within each.
#> ℹ The hazard is taken as constant within an interval, which biases the fit when
#>   temperature changes much within it. Failures at a known time are also given a
#>   short closing interval, so their hazard is that of the moment of failure.
#> ℹ Set `grid_dT` to change the step, or to `Inf` to keep the intervals as given.
models <- build_hazard_models("exp", c("mem", "weibull"),
                              dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + (1 | trial)))

# the bundle, written into a temporary folder here; rtft_source says the cluster
# installs rTFT from its repository on GitHub (by default it is read from how rTFT
# was installed on this machine)
bundle <- file.path(tempdir(), "my-run")
write_hpc_bundle(models, long, bundle, account = "def-someone", kfold = TRUE,
                 remote = "someone@nibi.alliancecan.ca:scratch/my-run",
                 rtft_source = "eogmartins/rTFT", chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 1)
#> ℹ Leaving out one trial at a time: the individuals of each trial share its
#>   effect in the model, so leaving out one individual would leave that effect in
#>   the fit.
#> ℹ Use `unit = "id"` to leave out individuals instead.
#> ✔ Wrote a bundle of 2 models to /tmp/Rtmp48sKkX/my-run: 2 fits and 4 refits for
#>   cross-validation, leaving out one trial at a time.
#> ℹ Copy it to the cluster with the command in step 1 of README.txt, in that
#>   folder.
#> ℹ Then, on the cluster, in that folder, run these two (the first once on each
#>   cluster):
#>   bash install.sh
#>   bash check.sh
list.files(bundle, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "README.txt"             "check.sh"               "inputs/checksums.txt"  
#>  [4] "inputs/data.rds"        "inputs/models.rds"      "inputs/settings.rds"   
#>  [7] "inputs/tasks-fit.csv"   "inputs/tasks-kfold.csv" "install.R"             
#> [10] "install.sh"             "settings.sh"            "status.sh"             
#> [13] "submit.sh"              "task.sh"
